descriptive_title: Grade 3 Mathematics: Algebra — Variables, Equivalent Expressions, and Equivalent Relationships for Whole Numbers to 1000 (C2.1-C2.3)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.C2.1: describe how variables are used, and use them in various contexts as appropriate
curriculum_expectations.C2.2: determine whether given pairs of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division expressions are equivalent or not
curriculum_expectations.C2.3: identify and use equivalent relationships for whole numbers up to 1000, in various contexts

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 3 unit on Algebra framed around 'Balanced Equations' — Eddy the Equation Engineer and Vex the Variable Vet. Day 1 introduces variables in real contexts (C2.1). Day 2 tests whether addition/subtraction expressions are equivalent (C2.2). Day 3 tests multiplication and division equivalence (C2.2). Day 4 hunts equivalent relationships for whole numbers up to 1000 (C2.3). Day 5 closes with child-created balance puzzles. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will describe and use variables; determine whether expressions across all four operations are equivalent; and find equivalent relationships for whole numbers up to 1000.

lesson_arc.big_idea: A variable stands for an unknown OR a quantity that varies. We use variables everywhere — temperature, score, age — when the value can change.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can describe how variables are used in real-life contexts.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Eddy introduces variables in temperature, sports scores, ages, prices; children identify variables in real-life examples.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Two addition or subtraction expressions are EQUIVALENT when they have the SAME total. 50+25 = 75 = 100-25.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can determine whether addition and subtraction expressions are equivalent.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children compare addition and subtraction expressions; sort EQUIVALENT vs NOT EQUIVALENT.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Two multiplication or division expressions are EQUIVALENT when they have the same product or quotient. 4x6 = 24 = 8x3 = 48÷2.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can determine whether multiplication and division expressions are equivalent.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children compare multiplication and division expressions; sort EQUIVALENT vs NOT EQUIVALENT.

lesson_arc.big_idea: There are MANY ways to make any whole number up to 1000. Mix all four operations.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can find many equivalent expressions for whole numbers up to 1000.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Equivalent-expression hunt across all four operations for target numbers (100, 250, 500, 750, 1000).

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can create balance puzzles using variables, equivalent expressions, and big numbers.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can create and solve a balance puzzle using a variable.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children invent a balance puzzle (e.g., 250 = 100 + ?); gallery share.

pedagogical_notes: C2.1 expands variables to include 'value that can change' (temperature, score) — not just unknown.
C2.2 across all 4 operations is the Grade-3 expansion. Use the balance scale to test each operation.
C2.3 to 1000 needs multiplication and division to be efficient. 100 = 25x4 = 50x2 = 200÷2.
The equal sign ALWAYS means SAME AMOUNT — across all operations.
Mix operations in equivalent expressions. Don't keep them in separate buckets.
canadian_context_notes: Real-life variables: temperature in Celsius (-30 to +30), Leafs score in a season, snowfall in cm per day, hockey goals scored.
Population: town populations up to 1000; equivalent expressions for population counts.
